newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Southern Cross reports NZ$2.2 mln yr net surplus.
newsitem.headline: Southern Cross reports NZ$2.2 mln yr net surplus.

text.p: Health insurer Southern Cross Healthcare on Tuesday reported an annual net surplus of $2.2 million, down from $6.6 million a year ago.
Its results for the year to June 30 showed a rise in demand for elective surgery and a payout of 98.2 cents in every dollar collected.
The non-profit organisation said contributions were up $34 million to $296 million in the year to June 30, 1996 and claims were up 16 percent to $290 million.
Southern Cross said demand for elective surgery rose 20 percent and played a big part in the overall claims growth.
The number of members claiming for surgery has grown by almost 50 percent in three years. In the last year Southern Cross paid out $140 million for surgery, up from $97 million in 1993/94.

The operating deficit of $19.50 million compared with a deficit of $13.16 million last year. Investment and other income of $21.73 million compared with $19.76 million last year contributed to the overall surplus.

Chairman Hylton LeGrice said the role of private health insurance in overall health financing in New Zealand was irreversible, but the number of people with private medical insurance had shrunk in recent years and the affordability of premiums was a continuing concern to the board.
While demand for medical services was growing, population changes meant that there were fewer younger members to recruit.
Southern Cross currently has nearly 900,000 members.
Southern Cross had net assets of $190.53 million at June 30, up from $188.30 million at the same time last year.
